programme.title: Marooned with Ed Stafford 2
programme.desc: Former British Army captain and experienced traveler Ed Stafford continues to overcome new challenges.He became known to viewers as a steadfast man who is able to cope with any extreme situation.So far, among others:he underwent a test of survival for 60 days on one of the uninhabited islands of Fiji, where he had no supplies of food, clothing or necessary equipment.Moreover, he walked the trail leading along the Amazon River, which earned him a place in history and the Guinness Book of Records.In the next series of the program "Ed Stafford Beyond Civilization", the traveler once again sets off to the most hostile corners of the world, including the Gobi Desert in Mongolia and the crocodile-infested Guatemalan jungle.

programme.title: Manhunt with Joel Lambert
programme.desc: Former Navy SEAL, Joel Lambert, faces an elite reconnaissance unit of the American army.Within two days, he must cover a specific route so as not to get caught.During this unusual mission, he can use the items he has in his backpack and what he finds along the way.Thanks to modern filming techniques, viewers follow the manhunt, both from the point of view of the hunted and the commandos tracking him.The program was shot in the United States, Poland, South Africa, the Philippines, Panama and South Korea.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: In Ethiopia, one and a half million people are blind.Martyna had the opportunity to meet representatives of the charity organization "Himalayan Cataract Project", which deals with free sight restoration for people from the poorest regions of the world.She accompanied several women in their everyday lives.The blind Muria, a nurse named Abeba, and the talented doctor Somega.The traveler had the opportunity to observe the course of eye surgery at the Ouiha hospital.She also attended a school for blind children in Mekele who learn Braille.They dream of being journalists and telling people about their life in Ethiopia.These dreams can come true thanks to the Himalayan Cataract Project foundation.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska and her team visit the Nyaru Menteng center, where orphaned orangutans find shelter.About sixty thousand representatives of this species live in Borneo.Their population is decreasing at an alarming rate, which is related to the devastation of the environment.At the Indonesian rehabilitation center, Martyna meets several exceptional women: the director of the center, Michelle, and the orangutan caregivers who take care of the little ones 24 hours a day and teach them the art of surviving in the wild.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: In picturesque Tanzania, the host will meet Naiyoma Rae, one of the few women pilots in Africa.The heroine of the episode lives in Arusha, but is rarely at home because she flies passenger planes almost every day and spends many hours in the clouds.Naiyoma is an extremely strong person who is not afraid of challenges.She will tell Martyna about, among other things, what animals disturb the most when landing and why, about her first solo flight and about numerous marriage offers from male passengers.In this episode, the host will also visit a coffee plantation, taste the sugar cane, and local women will do their hair according to the local fashion.

programme.title: Taste the world with Pascal
programme.desc: Pascal Brodnicki likes to explore the world through his sense of taste.He loves to prepare various dishes at street stalls, in African villages or on the beach. However, during his culinary journeys it was not always easy for him.Sometimes elephants stole his ingredients.Of course, Pascal couldn't deny himself the pleasure of tasting local delicacies.In Delhi, he stopped for a long time at a paratha stand, in a Zanzibar village he ate rice with coconut, and in Namibia he tried a zebra steak."Taste the world with Pascal" is not only about cooking.The host visited an elephant orphanage in Sri Lanka, fed cheetahs in Africa and climbed a coconut tree.In Bombay he became a teacher and taught Polish to children, and on the coast of Zanzibar he hunted octopus.Everywhere his passion and positive energy attracted crowds of onlookers.

programme.title: Taste the world with Pascal

However, during his culinary journeys it was not always easy for him.Sometimes elephants stole his ingredients.Of course, Pascal couldn't deny himself the pleasure of tasting local delicacies.In Delhi, he stopped for a long time at a paratha stand, in a Zanzibar village he ate rice with coconut, and in Namibia he tried a zebra steak."Taste the world with Pascal" is not only about cooking.The host visited an elephant orphanage in Sri Lanka, fed cheetahs in Africa and climbed a coconut tree.In Bombay he became a teacher and taught Polish to children, and on the coast of Zanzibar he hunted octopus.Everywhere his passion and positive energy attracted crowds of onlookers The next stage of the African journey is Zanzibar, a beautiful and multicultural island in the Indian Ocean.The local cuisine is a mix of many flavors from around the world.Pascal will go to the Forodhani market, famous for its delicious skewers with colorful stalls.He will discover the secrets of the plantain, also called "elephant's trunk", i.e. a sweet banana, which on the island is treated not as a fruit, but as a vegetable.Pascal will go octopus fishing.Zanzibar is also known for its colorful reefs, white sand, schools of rainbow fish and beautiful coastline.Pascal will set up his kitchen on one of such paradise beaches.This time, he will use a piece of a wooden boat as a countertop, and a natural rock depression filled with sea water as a sink.The chef will use local specialties and prepare seafood in spice sauce.He will invite a group of local women to his feast, who will return the favor with a dinner in a nearby village.

programme.title: Japan on a plate
programme.desc: Alexa Łuczak moved to the Land of the Rising Sun over ten years ago.During this time, she mastered the language on her own, which allowed her to host one of the local television programs.The model decided to share her knowledge about extraordinary Asian cuisine.Her search for local flavors will take her to small bars hidden in the city's alleys, to the largest fish market in Japan and to the establishments of the most talented sushi masters.The host will also visit elegant restaurants in Tokyo.There is no shortage of vending machines and fresh seafood in this city.Viewers will also learn more about Japan itself, its traditions and culture.
